By प्रभासाक्षी न्यूज़ डेस्क | Oct 14, 2026
उत्तराखंड के मुख्यमंत्री पुष्कर सिंह धामी ने राज्य के सभी जिलाधिकारियों (डीएम) और वरिष्ठ पुलिस अधीक्षकों (एसएसपी) के साथ बैठक कर विकास कार्यों, जनसुविधाओं, कानून-व्यवस्था और चुनाव संबंधी कार्यों की समीक्षा की। मुख्यमंत्री आवास पर मंगलवार को करीब चार घंटे तक चली इस बैठक में हरिद्वार कुंभ-2027 की तैयारियों पर भी चर्चा की गई। बैठक में गृह सचिव, गढ़वाल और कुमाऊं मंडलों के आयुक्त तथा दोनों पुलिस रेंज के पुलिस महानिरीक्षक समेत वरिष्ठ अधिकारी शामिल हुए।
उन्होंने सड़कों को गड्ढामुक्त बनाने के अभियान में तेजी लाने और निर्धारित समयसीमा के भीतर काम पूरा करने को कहा। मुख्यमंत्री ने कहा ‘‘मैं बहुत जल्द सड़क मार्ग से पूरे राज्य का व्यक्तिगत दौरा करूंगा। यदि कहीं क्षतिग्रस्त सड़कें मिलती हैं या मरम्मत कार्य में लापरवाही सामने आती है, तो संबंधित अधिकारी को जवाबदेह ठहराया जाएगा।’’ उन्होंने सीवर और पेयजल पाइपलाइन बिछाने के लिए खोदी गई सड़कों की स्थिति पर भी ध्यान देने तथा अधूरे कार्य एक नवंबर तक पूरे करने का निर्देश दिया।
मुख्यमंत्री ने पुलिस व्यवस्था को अधिक जवाबदेह, संवेदनशील और प्रभावी बनाने के निर्देश दिए। उन्होंने स्पष्ट किया कि संज्ञेय अपराधों की प्राथमिकी नियमानुसार तत्काल दर्ज की जाए और उसके बाद त्वरित एवं प्रभावी कार्रवाई की जाए। उन्होंने थानों और पुलिस चौकियों के प्रभारियों के कामकाज की नियमित समीक्षा करने तथा अपराध नियंत्रण, रात्रि गश्त, शिकायतों के निस्तारण और कानून-व्यवस्था बनाए रखने में लापरवाही के लिए जवाबदेही तय करने का भी निर्देश दिया।
इसके अलावा, शीतकालीन पर्यटन को ध्यान में रखते हुए मुख्यमंत्री ने मसूरी, नैनीताल, हरिद्वार और ऋषिकेश समेत राज्य के प्रमुख पर्यटन एवं धार्मिक स्थलों के लिए पहले से यातायात योजनाएं तैयार करने को कहा।

Heavy rain likely in Kerala as northeast monsoon sets in tomorrow, orange alert in 4 districts
Thiruvananthapuram: Kerala is likely to receive heavy to very heavy rainfall over the coming days as the northeast monsoon is set to commence over the southern peninsula on Thursday, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said on Wednesday.
The weather department has issued an orange alert in Pathanamthitta, Kottayam, Ernakulam and Idukki districts for October 15, warning of very heavy rainfall. A yellow alert has been issued in eight other districts for the day. An orange alert indicates very heavy rainfall of 12 cm to 20 cm in 24 hours, while a yellow alert indicates heavy rainfall of 7 cm to 11 cm.
The IMD said conditions were becoming favourable for the withdrawal of the southwest monsoon from the remaining parts of the country and the simultaneous onset of northeast monsoon rains over the southern peninsula on October 15.
According to the forecast, isolated places in Kerala are likely to receive heavy to very heavy rainfall of 7 cm to 20 cm on Thursday. Heavy rainfall is also likely at isolated places from October 16 to 20. The IMD has also forecast thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds in the state over the coming days.
On October 15 and 16, thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and winds reaching 40-50 kmph are likely at one or two places. Similar conditions, with wind speeds of 30-40 kmph, are expected at isolated places on October 14, 17 and 18.
The weather department attributed the conditions to an upper-air cyclonic circulation over central parts of Kerala and adjoining areas at an altitude of 4.5 km above mean sea level, along with another circulation over the Comorin region and neighbourhood.
Thunderstorms accompanied by lightning are also likely at one or two places in Lakshadweep from October 14 to 16.

During the storm affecting Santiago, the capital of Chile, a tornado that formed in the Estación Central area blew off the roofs of the Terminal Sur bus station and surrounding buildings. Chile's Meteorological Directorate announced that, according to initial analyses, the event could be an EF0 category tornado. In the city, where hail, flooding, and power outages occurred, the National Disaster Prevention and Response Service (Senapred) declared a red alert. Terrifying moments on camera.
On the day when downpours, hail, and a storm were effective in Santiago, the tornado in Estacion Central caused terrifying moments. The moments when torn-off roof pieces were blown through the air were recorded with mobile phone cameras.
THE BUS TERMINAL'S ROOF FLEW THROUGH THE AIR
In the Estacion Central commune, around Alameda Avenue at about 16:30 local time, strong wind formed. The wind tore off part of the roof of Terminal Sur, one of the city's important bus terminals. In the footage, roof sheets and light materials were seen being blown to distant distances.
Due to the tornado, damage occurred to the roofs, gutters, and cladding of surrounding buildings, and some tiles fell. It was reported that shallow-rooted trees were uprooted and tree branches were broken. No information was shared regarding whether anyone was injured or lost their lives in the incident.
METEOROLOGY: THERE MAY BE AN EF0 CATEGORY TORNADO
The Chilean Meteorological Directorate (DMC), in a statement on its social media account, said, “Initial analyses indicate that the event could be an EF0 category tornado.” According to the agency's preliminary report, wind speed was estimated at between 105 and 137 kilometers per hour. DMC stated that the exact classification of the event has not yet been made and that investigations are ongoing.
DMC meteorologist Elio Brufort reported that atmospheric instability and high temperatures during the day fueled vertically developing clouds, downpours, hail, and this event.
“NO FUNNEL CLOUD IS VISIBLE” ASSESSMENT
The Chilean Geosciences Network (Red Geocientífica de Chile), on the other hand, suggested that the event may not be a tornado but a sudden wind vortex (gustnado) or a sudden and strong downdraft (microburst). The organization assessed, “In the visual records, no funnel cloud or connection of the storm to the ground by a vortex is seen.”
RED ALERT ISSUED IN THE CITY
Senapred declared a red alert for the entire Metropolitan Region where Santiago is located at 17:15 local time. The Meteorological Directorate also issued a storm warning for 7 regions stretching from Coquimbo to Biobio.
Heavy hail fell in many parts of the city, main streets and underpasses were flooded. In Providencia, the roofs of some parking lots collapsed and fell onto vehicles. Pedro de Valdivia and Salvador stations on the Metro line were closed due to flooding, and services on Line 2 could be partially operated. Education was suspended in schools.
7 REGIONS LEFT WITHOUT ELECTRICITY
According to data from the Chilean Electricity and Fuel Superintendency (SEC), the number of customers affected by outages exceeded 43,000. Quilicura, Quinta Normal, Providencia, Lampa, Pudahuel, and Estacion Central were among the areas most affected by the outages.
A few days earlier, a flood disaster had also occurred in Santiago; in the flood that occurred in San Carlos de Apoquindo, 6 people were injured and more than 2,000 homes were affected.
